images.title: Moving between units
images.purpose: Recap that changing to a smaller unit multiplies and changing to a bigger unit divides, using a simple length staircase.
images.composition: A four step staircase going down from left to right in the centre of the frame, with multiply arrows on the way down and divide arrows on the way up, and one example line at the bottom.
exact_structure: 4 flat steps going down from left to right, each a rounded box: 'km' (top left), 'm', 'cm', 'mm' (bottom right)
Step boxes coloured teal #0072B2 outline with white fill
3 green #009E73 down arrows on the lower side of the staircase: km to m '× 1000', m to cm '× 100', cm to mm '× 10'
3 vermilion #D55E00 up arrows on the upper side of the staircase: mm to cm '÷ 10', cm to m '÷ 100', m to km '÷ 1000'
1 reddish purple #CC79A7 example line at the bottom centre: '1.2 m = 120 cm'
rejection: any conversion factor attached to the wrong pair of units
the multiply arrows pointing up the staircase instead of down
any example other than 1.2 m = 120 cm
images.takeaway: Going to a smaller unit, multiply; going to a bigger unit, divide; then check the answer is a sensible size.
images.description: A staircase of km, m, cm and mm with times 1000, 100 and 10 arrows going down and matching divide arrows going up, with the example 1.2 m = 120 cm.
images.context: Shown beside the everyday decimal problems practice.
images.teaching_notes: Before each problem, decide whether you move down the stairs (multiply) or up (divide).

image_decisions.why: A unit staircase is a quick visual recap of when to multiply and when to divide in the practice problems.
